meta.description: Evaluate scientific claims and evidence quality. Use for assessing experimental design validity, identifying biases and confounders, applying evidence grading frameworks (GRADE, Cochrane Risk of Bias), or teaching critical analysis. Best for understanding evidence quality and identifying flaws. Provides systematic process for evaluating scientific rigor.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated methodological claims; accurate representation of GRADE and Cochrane ROB frameworks

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for critical analysis with clear guidance on constructive, specific, proportionate evaluation

methodological_ground.detail: Based on established evidence-grading frameworks (GRADE, Cochrane) and critical thinking principles

code_usability.detail: No code generation in this analytical guidance skill

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of critical thinking: methodology critique, bias detection, statistical evaluation, evidence quality, logical fallacies

reliability.note: Excellent reliability with systematic 7-capability framework, application guidelines (constructive, specific, proportionate, consistent)

performance_context.note: Well-organized with core capabilities documentation, 6 reference files covering methods, biases, statistics, evidence hierarchy, fallacies, design

agent_usability.note: Outstanding with When to Use section, 7-capability framework, clear application guidelines, GRADE/Cochrane framework integration

human_usability.note: Clear guidance structure with application guidelines; minor: no installation or setup section (analytical skill, but clarity could be improved)

security.note: Good security with optional figure generation via scientific-schematics (API disclosure); minor: no explicit guidance on handling unpublished data

maintainability.note: Version 1.2, MIT license, clear reference structure with 6 topic-specific files

agent_specific.note: Strong with clear trigger (evaluate scientific claims), scientific-schematics integration; minor: boundary to peer-review skill mentioned but criteria for choosing not detailed

inputs.label: Evaluate experimental design and identify confounders

assertions.note: Core capability: design, controls, confounding
Application guideline: 'Point to specific instances'
Be Constructive: 'Identify strengths as well as weaknesses'
Be Proportionate: 'Distinguish between fatal flaws and minor limitations'

inputs.label: Apply GRADE framework to systematic review evidence

assertions.note: Explicitly listed as core capability
Core capability 4: study hierarchy, replication, strength of inference
When to Use: 'Conducting systematic reviews or meta-analyses'
Evidence hierarchy reference covers GRADE domains

inputs.label: Identify statistical p-hacking and multiplicity issues

assertions.note: Core capability 3: power, multiplicity, p-value misuse, effect sizes
Dedicated reference file for statistical issues
Multiplicity listed in capability description
P-value misuse and effect sizes both listed

inputs.label: Detect logical fallacies in research argument

assertions.note: Core capability 5: fallacies that recur in scientific argument
Dedicated reference file
Core capability 7: separating what was shown from what is asserted
Reference mentioned but specific examples not shown in main SKILL.md

inputs.label: Write formal peer review report for journal

assertions.note: 'For formal peer review writing use peer-review'
When to Use: 'Providing critical analysis of research papers'
Explicit redirection provided
Boundary stated but not when to use which skill

key_strengths: Comprehensive 7-capability framework covering methodology, bias, statistics, evidence quality, fallacies, design guidance, and claim evaluation
Excellent application guidelines with 4 clear principles: be constructive, specific, proportionate, and apply consistent standards
Strong integration of established frameworks (GRADE, Cochrane Risk of Bias) with dedicated reference documentation
Outstanding systematic approach with 6 topic-specific reference files providing depth beyond main SKILL.md
Good composability with scientific-schematics skill for optional flowchart/framework diagrams

recommendations.title: Add example logical fallacies to main documentation
recommendations.problem: Logical fallacies mentioned but no inline examples provided
recommendations.root_cause: Agent usability: common patterns not immediately accessible
recommendations.fix: Add to ## Core Capabilities: 'Common scientific fallacies: appeal to authority (expert ≠ evidence), post hoc ergo propter hoc (correlation ≠ causation), Texas sharpshooter (cherry-picking data).'

recommendations.title: Clarify critical-thinking vs peer-review skill boundary
recommendations.problem: Boundary stated but decision criteria not provided
recommendations.fix: Add note: 'Use scientific-critical-thinking for analyzing methodology and evidence. Use peer-review for structured journal review format with accept/revise/reject framing.'

recommendations.title: Add guidance on handling unpublished data
recommendations.problem: Optional figure generation uses API but data handling not addressed
recommendations.root_cause: Security criterion: sensitive data handling could be more explicit
recommendations.fix: Add to ## Visual Aids disclosure: 'When analyzing unpublished research, do not include proprietary methods, unpublished results, or confidential details in figure prompts sent to external APIs.'
